Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — we had a couple of follow-ups from Security and Legal about the hosted API data lifecycle. Can you confirm the answers to the items below? We need this to close our internal risk assessment.

1) Residency: when a tenant selects an EU region, does all request content and metadata persist only in that region (including logs/backups)?
2) Deletion windows: if we request a tenant-level purge or an object-level erase, what is the expected timeline for (a) primary storage purges and (b) removal from backups/snapshots?
3) Proof of deletion: do you provide attestations or an audit record showing deletion events (timestamps, operator id, request id)?
4) Legal holds: can Redwood place an account on a retention hold (preserve data) and later release it? How are holds reconciled with automated TTLs?
5) For troubleshooting we occasionally ask for short-term retention beyond default TTLs — is there an opt-in mechanism and an approval workflow?

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answers below (high level) and I attached a concise diagram + our deletion runbook for detail. Happy to walk through any item on a call.

1) Residency
- Default behavior: when a customer selects an EU region for their tenant, request payloads, generated outputs, and request-level metadata are stored and processed in that region. Control plane metadata that is purely billing/operational may be stored in our control-plane region, but we keep tenant data separate.
- Backups/snapshots: backups of primary storage are retained in-region by default. Cross-region replication only occurs if configured for DR and is explicit in the order form.

2) Deletion windows
- Primary storage: for a standard hosted-API tenant, an explicit deletion request (tenant or object-level) triggers immediate removal from live primary storage; most objects are removed within 48 hours depending on the size of the dataset and active shard compaction.
- Backups/snapshots: snapshots are immutable; after a deletion request we mark relevant snapshot segments and schedule background compaction/rewrites — full removal from backup storage can take up to 30 days (we provide a retention-exception timeline in the runbook).

3) Proof of deletion
- We emit auditable deletion events into the tenant's audit log: deletion_request_id, initiating_principal (internal operator or API key), timestamp, and affected object ids. We can provide an attestation package (signed audit excerpt) for compliance reviews.

4) Legal/Retention holds
- Redwood supports account-level legal holds. When a hold is placed we pause automated TTL-based purges for the affected data class. Holds are surfaced in our admin console and require a named approver to add/remove. Holds can be scoped (e.g., by dataset tag or time-range).

5) Short-term extended retention
- We provide a "diagnostic retention" opt-in (30/90 day options) for troubleshooting. This is controlled by the customer via Console or by a signed request routed through Support/SRE; approval is logged and the retention change is auditable.

Attachments: data_flow_diagram.pdf (high-level flow showing region boundaries), deletion_runbook.pdf (detailed timelines, compaction windows, and attestation process).

Links: SOC 2 report and DPA are linked here: https://redwood.ai/compliance/soc2-report/latest and https://app.redwood.ai/dpa/medigroup-eu

If you want an SLA commitment for purge completion we can scope that in the DPA/Order Form — standard hosted tiers don't include a deletion SLA, but we offer SLA add-ons for enterprise/dedicated customers.

Hi Elena — quick follow-up from Product/Compliance side.

- Status updates: when we initiate a tenant/object purge we create a unique purge request id and a ticket in our incident system. Customers with enterprise support can use the purge id to query a read-only status endpoint (example: GET /purges/{purge_id}) which returns stages (initialized, primary_purged, backup_compaction_pending, backup_purged) and timestamps. For hosted customers without the enterprise add-on we provide ticket updates via Support and a signed attestation once purging completes.

- Legal holds API: currently holds are console- and Support-driven. We are rolling out a programmatic API for holds in Q1 2029 (scoped to enterprise customers). For Medigroup we can enable the API early under an addendum — we will need a signed DPA + approval from Compliance.

Next steps I propose:
1) Sergio — I can send Medigroup the standard hold/retention addendum and a sample purge-attestation template.
2) If Medigroup wants an SLA for deletion completion we should scope it in the Order Form (we typically commit enterprise purge completion within 72 hours for primary + 30 days for backup purges; we can tighten the primary window for an additional fee).
3) Offer to schedule a 30-minute technical run-through with Naomi (security compliance lead) and an SRE to walk the runbook.

Elena, would Thursday next week work for a short call? I can send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
